chunks: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh al-Qummi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan, Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Musa al-Daqqaq, and Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Sinani (may Allah be pleased with them) narrated to us. They said: Abu'l-Abbas Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Zakariyya al-Qattan narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Abbas narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Abi al-Sirri narrated to me. He said: Ahmad ibn Abdullah ibn Yunus narrated to us, from Sa'd ibn Tarif al-Kinani, from al-Asbagh ibn Nubata. He said: When

Ali (peace be upon him) assumed the Caliphate and the people pledged their allegiance to him. He went out to the Mosque, turbaned with the turban of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), clothed in the cloak of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), wearing the sandals of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and girded with the sword of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). He ascended the pulpit and sat upon it firmly. Then he interlaced his fingers

He placed [his hands] at the lower part of his abdomen, then said: 'O assembly of people, ask me before you lose me! This is the vessel of knowledge, this is the saliva of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him and his family), this is what the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him and his family) fed me morsel by morsel! Ask me, for I have the knowledge of the ancients and the latter ones. By Allah, if the cushion were folded for me and I sat upon it, I would surely give rulings to the people of the Torah according to their Torah until the Torah itself would speak and say: Ali has spoken the truth — he has not lied; he has issued rulings to you according to what Allah revealed in me! And I would give rulings to the people of the Gospel according to their Gospel until the Gospel itself would speak and say: Ali has spoken the truth — he has not lied; he has issued rulings to you according to what Allah revealed in me! And I would give rulings to the people of the Quran according to their Quran until the Quran itself would speak and say: Ali has spoken the truth — he has not lied; he has issued rulings to you according to what Allah revealed in me! While you recite the Quran night and day, is there anyone among you who knows what was revealed in it? Were it not for a verse in the Book of Allah the Mighty and Majestic, I would surely inform you of what was, what will be, and what exists until the Day of Resurrection — and it is this verse: {Allah erases what He wills and confirms [what He wills], and with Him is the Mother of the Book} (13:39). Then he (peace be upon him) said: Ask me before you lose me, by [Him who]...'

By Him who split the grain and created the living soul: if you had asked me about any verse — whether it was revealed at night or by day, Meccan or Medinan, revealed during travel or at home, its abrogating or abrogated verses, its unambiguous or ambiguous passages, its inner interpretation or the context of its revelation — I would have informed you. Then a man known as Dhi'lib al-Yamani came forward — he was sharp of tongue, eloquent in speeches, and bold of heart. He said: 'Verily the son of Abu Talib has mounted a difficult step; I shall embarrass him today before you with my question.' He said: 'O Commander of the Believers, have you seen your Lord?' He replied: 'Woe to you, O Dhi'lib! I would not be one who worships a Lord I have not seen.' He asked: 'But how did you see Him? Describe Him to us.' He replied: 'Woe to you! The eyes do not perceive Him through direct visual sight, but the hearts perceive Him through the realities of faith. Woe to you, O Dhi'lib! Verily my Lord cannot be described as distant, nor as moving, nor as still, nor as standing erect, nor as coming, nor as going. Subtle is His subtlety — He cannot be described with ordinary subtlety; Great is His greatness — He cannot be

described with [ordinary] greatness; Majestic is His majesty — He cannot be described with ordinary bigness; Glorious is His glory — He cannot be described with coarseness; Compassionate is His mercy — He cannot be described with ordinary tenderness; the Faithful Believer (al-Mu'min) — not through [ordinary] worship

Perceiver — not through touch; Speaker — not through vocal utterance. He is within things — but not in a manner of commingling; outside things — but not in a manner of total separation. Above all things — and nothing can be said to be above Him; before all things — and nothing before can be said to precede Him. Within things — not as a thing is within a thing; and outside them — not as a thing is outside another thing. Then Dhi'lib fell into a faint, and then said: 'By God, I have never heard anything like this answer — by God I shall never again ask such a question.' Then Ali (peace be upon him) said: 'Ask me before you lose me.' So al-Ash'ath ibn Qays stood up toward him and said: 'O Commander of the Believers, how is jizyah taken from the Zoroastrians when no scripture was revealed to them and no prophet was sent to them?' He replied: 'Yes indeed, O Ash'ath! God did reveal a scripture unto them and did send a prophet to them. And they had a king who became drunk one night and summoned his daughter to his bed and committed [sin] with her. When morning came, word spread among his people and they gathered [before his door].

He said to them: 'Do you know that God, Mighty and Majestic, created no creature more honoured to Him than our father Adam and our mother Eve?' They said: 'You have spoken truly, O king.' He said: 'Did He not then marry His sons to His daughters, and His daughters to His sons?' They said: 'You have spoken truly — this is the religion.' So they made a pact upon that. Then God erased what was in their hearts of knowledge and removed the scripture from them. So they are the disbelievers — they enter the Fire without reckoning; and the hypocrites are in a worse state than them. Al-Ash'ath said: 'By God, I have never heard anything like this answer — by God I shall never return to the like of it ever.' Then Ali (peace be upon him) said: 'Ask me before you lose me.' So a man from the farthest end of the mosque stood up toward him, leaning on a staff, making his way through the people until he drew near to him and said: 'O Commander of the Believers, guide me to a deed that, if I do it, God will save me from the Fire.' So he said to him: 'Listen, O you, then understand, then be certain: the world stands by three — a scholar who speaks out and acts upon his knowledge, and a wealthy person who does not

withholds his wealth from the people of God's religion, Mighty and Majestic; and a poor person who is patient. For when the scholar conceals his knowledge, and the wealthy is miserly, and the poor person does not have patience — then at that point woe and destruction! And then those who truly know God will recognize that the world has reverted to its beginning — that is, to disbelief after faith. O questioner, do not be deceived by the multitude of mosques and the congregation of people whose bodies are together but whose hearts are scattered. O people, people are of three types: the ascetic (zahid), the worldly-desirer (raghib), and the patient (sabir). As for the ascetic — he neither rejoices over anything of the world that comes to him, nor grieves over anything of it that eludes him. As for the patient one — he yearns for it in his heart, but if he attains any of it, he turns himself away from it because of what he knows of the evil of its consequences. As for the worldly-desirer — he does not care whether he obtains it from halal or haram. He said: 'O Commander of the Believers, then what is the sign of the believer in that era?' He replied: 'He looks to what God has made obligatory upon him of what is right and allies with it, and looks at what opposes it and disavows it, even if it be a beloved and close relative.' The man said: 'You have spoken truly, by God, O Commander of the Believers.' Then the man disappeared and people searched for him but could not find him. So Ali (peace be upon him) smiled on the pulpit and then said:

What is the matter with you? — this is my brother al-Khidr (AS). Then he (AS) said: Ask me before you lose me. But no one stood up to him. So he praised God and extolled Him, and invoked blessings upon His Prophet (SAWA). Then he said to al-Hasan (AS): O Hasan, rise and ascend the pulpit, and speak with such words that Quraysh will not consider you ignorant after my passing. Al-Hasan (AS) said: O my father, how can I ascend and speak while you are among the people, listening and watching? He (AS) said: May my father and mother be your ransom — I will conceal myself from you, listening and watching, but you will not see me. So al-Hasan (AS) ascended the pulpit, praised God with eloquent and noble praises, invoked blessings upon the Prophet and his family with a concise prayer, then said: O people, I heard my grandfather the Messenger of God (SAWA) say: I am the city of knowledge and Ali is its gate — and does one enter the city except through its gate? Then he descended, and Ali (AS) leaped toward him, embraced him, and held him to his chest. Then he said to al-Husayn (AS): O my son, rise and ascend and speak with such words that Quraysh will not say al-Husayn ibn Ali knows nothing

sees nothing; and let your speech follow your brother's speech. So al-Husayn (AS) ascended the pulpit, praised God and extolled Him, and invoked blessings upon His Prophet and his family with a concise prayer, then said: O assembly of people, I heard the Messenger of God (SAWA) say: Ali is the city of guidance — whoever enters it is saved, and whoever stays away from it perishes. Then Ali (AS) leaped up and held him close to his chest and kissed him. Then he said: O assembly of people, bear witness that these two are the two chicks of the Messenger of God (SAWA) and his trust which he entrusted to me — and I now entrust it to you, O assembly of people, and the Messenger of God (SAWA) will ask you about them both.

key_terms.أُمُّ الْكِتَابِ: The Mother of the Book — the primordial preserved tablet (Lawh al-Mahfuz)
key_terms.الزَّاهِد: The ascetic — one who has renounced worldly attachments
key_terms.الْجِزْيَة: Jizya — the poll-tax levied on non-Muslim subjects of an Islamic state
key_terms.سِفْطُ الْعِلْمِ: Vessel/chest of knowledge — metaphor for one who contains all knowledge
key_terms.مَدِينَةُ الْعِلْمِ: City of Knowledge — famous hadith designating the Prophet as the city and Ali as its gate

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say in his first sermon after assuming the caliphate?
ai.summary: This is a pivotal narration from al-Amali of Shaykh al-Saduq, transmitted through al-Asbagh ibn Nubata, a close companion of Imam Ali (AS). It describes Imam Ali's first sermon after assuming the caliphate, delivered while wearing the Prophet's turban, cloak, sandals, and sword — symbolizing his legitimate succession. In the sermon, the Imam declared his vast knowledge of all scriptures and the Quran, answered profound theological questions about the nature of God (in a response that rendered the questioner Dhi'lb unconscious), explained the historical basis for jizya from Zoroastrians, described three types of people and the conditions of the world, and concluded by directing his sons al-Hasan and al-Husayn to the pulpit where they cited the famous hadith of the 'City of Knowledge.'

en.bilal-muhammad: Abu Ja`far Muhammad b. `Ali b. al-Husayn b. Musa b. Babuwayh al-Qummi (ra) narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. al-Hasan al-Qattan and `Ali b. Ahmad b. Musa al-Daqqaq and Muhammad b. Ahmad al-Sinani (ra) narrated to us. They said: Abu’l `Abbas Ahmad b. Yahya b. Zakariyya al-Qattan narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-`Abbas narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Abi al-Sirri narrated to me. He said: Ahmad b. `Abdullah b. Yunus narrated to us from Sa`d b. Turayf al-Kinani from al-Asbagh b. Nubata. He said: When

`Ali (as) assumed the Caliphate and the people pledged their allegiance to him, he went out to the Mosque turbaned in the turban of the Messenger of Allah (s), cloaked in the cloak of the Messenger of Allah (s), wearing the sandals of the Messenger of Allah (s), and equipped with the sword of the Messenger of Allah (s). So, he climbed the pulpit and sat upon it masterfully. Then, he folded his hands

and placed them under his stomach. Then, he said: O people! Ask me before you lose me. This is the vessel of knowledge. This is the saliva of the Messenger of Allah (s). This is the sustenance that the Messenger of Allah (s) has sustained me with. Ask me, for I have the knowledge of the former and latter peoples. By Allah, if a cushion were folded for me, I could give judgments to the people of the Torah with their Torah until the Torah is made to say: “`Ali has spoken the truth and he has not lied. He has given you judgments by that which Allah has revealed”; and I could give judgments to the people of the Gospel with their Gospel until the Gospel is made to say: “`Ali has spoken the truth and he has not lied. He has given you judgments by that which Allah has revealed”; and I could give judgments to the people of the Quran with their Quran until the Quran is made to say: “`Ali has spoken the truth and he has not lied. He has given you judgments by that which Allah has revealed.” You recite the Quran night and day, so, is there one of you who knows what was revealed in it? If it were not for one verse in the Book of Allah, I could have informed you of what was, what will be, and what is, until the Day of Resurrection; and it is this verse, “Allah erases what He wishes and confirms, and with Him is the Mother of the Book.” [13:39] Then, he (as) said: Ask me before you lose me, for by Him who split the seed and gave life,

if you were to ask me about any verse – whether it were revealed in the night or revealed in the day, in Mecca or in Medina, while travelling or while present; whether it is abrogating or abrogated, decisive or allegorical; or about its interpretation or its exegesis – I would have informed you of it.  So, a man named Dha`lab, who had a sharp tongue, who was eloquent in speech, and who had a bold heart, said: Ibn Abi Talib has risen to a difficult station, so I will embarrass him today in my questions posed to him. So, he said: O Amir al-Mu’minin! Have you seen your Lord? So, he said: Woe to you, Dha`lab, I am not one who would worship a Lord that I haven not seen. He said: So, how did you see Him? Describe Him to us. He said: Woe to you! Eyes do not see Him by way of sight, but rather, hearts see Him by the realities of faith. Woe to you, Dha`lab, surely, my Lord is not described with proximity, nor with movement, nor with stillness, nor with standing – standing physically – nor with coming, nor with going. He is the Most Subtle of the subtle, but He is not described with subtlety. He is the Most Great of the great, but He is not described with greatness. He is the Most Grand of the grand, but He is not described with grandness. He is the Most Majestic of the majestic, but He is not described with difficulty. He is kind in mercy, but He is not described with gentleness; the Protector, but not [gained] through worship.

He perceives, but not through touching. He speaks, but not through pronouncement. He is in the things, but not interwoven, and He is outside of them, but not contrasting. He is above everything, and nothing is to be said to be above Him. He is in front of everything, but He is not to be said to be in front. He is inside the things, but not like a thing inside another thing. He is outside the things, but not like a thing outside another thing. So, Dha`lab fell unconscious. Then, [he awoke] and said: By Allah, I have never heard an answer like this. By Allah, I will not repeat [a question] like it. Then, he (as) said: Ask me before you lose me. So, al-Ash`ath b. Qays went to him and said: O Amir al-Mu’minin! Why is the jizya taken from the Zoroastrians when no Book was revealed to them and no prophet was sent to them? So, he said: O Ash`ath! Allah revealed a Book to them and sent a prophet to them. They had a king who was drunk one night. He called his daughter to his bed and had intercourse with her. When he awoke, his people had heard what had happened and had gathered at his door. So, they said: “O king! You have dirtied our religion and you have destroyed it. Get out, so that we may purify you by establishing the penalty on you.” So, he said to them: “Gather and listen to my words. If there is no way out for me, then do as you wish.” So, they gathered. So, he said to them: “Do you know that Allah did not create a creation more noble than our father Adam and our mother Hawwa’?” They said: “You have spoken the truth, king.” He said: “Did he not marry his sons to his daughters, and his daughters to his sons?” They said: “You have spoken the truth. This is the religion.” So, they contracted [marriages] based on that. So, Allah erased knowledge from their hearts and raised the Book from them, so they became disbelievers who enter the Fire without judgment – and the hypocrites are in a more severe condition than them. So, al-Ash`ath said: By Allah, I have never heard an answer like this. By Allah, I will not repeat [a question] like it.  Then, he (as) said: Ask me before you lose me. So, a man from the furthest end of the Mosque came to him, leaning on a staff. He did not stop surpassing the people until he came close to him and said: O Amir al-Mu’minin! Lead me to a practice which, if I did it, Allah would deliver me from the Fire. So, he said to him: Listen, so-and-so, then understand, then ascertain. The world is upheld by three: a speaking scholar whose knowledge is acted upon, a wealthy person who is not stingy in his wealth with the people of the religion of Allah, and patient poor person. If the scholar hides his knowledge, and the wealthy becomes stingy, and the poor person is not patient, then at that will be woe and devastation. At that, those that know Allah will know that the abode will revert to its incipience – meaning, to disbelief after faith. O asker! Do not be deceived by the number of mosques, nor by the gatherings of people who are united in their bodies but disunited in their hearts. O people! Surely, there are only three types of people: the ascetic, the hedonist, and the patient. As for the ascetic, he is not gladdened by anything of the world that comes to him, nor is he saddened by anything of the world that misses him. As for the patient, he wishes for it (the world) in his heart, but when he comes by anything of it, he avoids it because he knows its evil consequences. As for the hedonist, he does not mind taking it lawfully or unlawfully.  He said: O Amir al-Mu’minin! What is the sign of the believer in that time? He said: He looks to what Allah has obliged him and he fulfills it, and he looks to what is contrary to it and dissociates from it, even if it is beloved and near to him. He said: You have spoken the truth, by Allah, O Amir al-Mu’minin. Then, the man disappeared, and we did not see him. The people went out looking for him, but they did not see him. So, `Ali (as) smiled on the pulpit and said:

What are you doing? This is my brother al-Khidr (as). Then, he (as) said: Ask me before you lose me. So, no one went to him. So, he praised Allah and commended Him, blessed His Prophet (s), then said to al-Hasan (as): O Hasan! Stand, climb the pulpit, and speak, so that Quraysh are not ignorant of you after me, lest they say: “Al-Hasan has not beautified (yuhsin) anything.” Al-Hasan (as) said: O father! How can I climb [the pulpit] and speak when you are among the people listening and watching? He said: May my mother and my father be your sacrifice! I will hide myself from you, so you will neither hear nor see me. So, al-Hasan (as) climbed the pulpit, praised Allah in an eloquent and honourable way, blessed the Prophet and his Family briefly, then said: O people! I heard my grandfather the Messenger of Allah (s) say: “I am the City of Knowledge and `Ali is its Gate. A city can only be entered by its gate.” Then, he descended; and `Ali (as) leapt toward him, embraced him, and held him to his chest. Then, he said to al-Husayn (as): O my son! Stand, climb the pulpit, and speak, so that the Quraysh are not ignorant of you after me, lest they say: “Al-Husayn b. `Ali has no insight in anything”, and so that your words may follow your brother’s. So, al-Husayn climbed, praised Allah and commended Him, blessed His Prophet and his Family briefly, then said: O people! I heard the Messenger of Allah (s) say: “Surely, `Ali is the City of Guidance. Whoever enters it is saved, and whoever turns away from it is destroyed.” So, `Ali (as) leapt toward him, embraced him, and held him to his chest. Then, he said: O people! Bear witness that these two are the younglings of the Messenger of Allah (s) whom he entrusted to me, and I am entrusting them to you. O people! The Messenger of Allah (s) will question you regarding them.
